regime.label: Short-gamma gap to the 1100 flip narrows to 34 points as the Protection build decelerates, 80 DTE
evidence: Cumulative net GEX turns positive only above the 1100 gamma flip; spot at 1065.9 sits 34.1 points below it, the narrowest gap of the 5-day window (down from 44.9 on 07-10 and roughly 60 on 07-09), so dealers stay net short gamma even as the gap keeps closing.

The far 910 put strike added just 108 contracts (+2.4%) to 4,644 on 130 lots today, a much quieter build than 07-10's 937-contract (+26%) spike on 1,153 lots - the Protection flow continues but is decelerating.

P/C OI ratio hit a fresh 5-day high of 1.42 (from 1.32), even as call OI still outweighs put OI by 4,418 contracts in the immediate 1040-1110 band (down from 5,048 yesterday), a locally dampening tilt keeping price under the 1080 wall.
ATM IV eased to 14.47% (from 14.86%) and the 25-delta skew narrowed to 2.63 (from 2.9), both inside the week's 13.79-15.03% / 1.78-2.90 ranges - no compression or expansion trend at 80 DTE.

S50U26.today_summary: SET50 Sep futures (S50U26) closed at 1065.9, +10.9 points (+1.03%), the second straight up session and now 34.1 points below the 1100 cumulative gamma flip - the narrowest gap of the 5-day window (from 44.9 on 07-10). The far 910 put strike added a modest 108 contracts (+2.4%) to 4,644 on 130 lots, far quieter than 07-10's 937-contract spike, yet the P/C OI ratio still pushed to a fresh 5-day high of 1.42. Call OI continues to outweigh put OI by 4,418 contracts in the immediate 1040-1110 band (down from 5,048 yesterday), keeping the tape locally dampened under the 1080 call wall. ATM IV eased to 14.47% (from 14.86%), still inside the week's 13.79-15.03% range.
what_changed: 910 put OI +108 contracts (+2.4%) to 4,644 on 130-lot volume, a much quieter build than 07-10's 937-contract (+26%) spike.
P/C OI ratio +0.10 to a fresh 5-day high of 1.42; P/C volume ratio eased to 1.02 from 1.18 as call volume picked up relative to puts.
Futures +10.9 points (+1.03%) to 1065.9, narrowing the gap to the 1100 gamma flip to 34.1 points from 44.9 the prior session.
Near-put support rolled to 1040 from 1050 the prior session; the 1080 call wall held for a third day (1,844 -> 1,878 OI, +34).
S50U26.five_day_thesis: Max pain has held in the 1040-1050 band for all 5 sessions (1040 on 07-07/08/09/10, then 1050 today) despite futures swinging from 1057.7 (07-08) down to 1040.4 (07-09) and back up to 1065.9 today - a 25.5-point round trip on only 10 points of max-pain drift, confirming the anchor is structural rather than a live target at 80 DTE. The cumulative gamma flip has migrated up from 1080-1090 (07-07) through 1090-1100 (07-09/07-10) to 1100-1110 today, tracking the put build, while spot has stayed under it every session - the gap has narrowed from roughly 60 points on 07-09 to 34.1 points today, the tightest of the window. Total put OI is up 30.9% from 11,118 (07-07) to 14,557 today, with the 910 tail-put strike alone growing 44.2% (3,220 to 4,644), though today's +2.4% add is the smallest daily increment of the run after 07-10's 26% spike. ATM IV stayed range-bound (13.79-15.03%) all week with no directional trend, and the 25-delta skew oscillated 1.78-2.90 (2.63 today), so the put build reads as steady hedging demand, not a fear spike. The 1080 call wall has been the single most stable structural level all week (OI 1,700 -> 1,878, always the largest call strike) and is the level to watch for the first real test of the narrowing short-gamma gap.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1030P / 990P
strategies.rationale: Put OI grew 30.9% over 5 sessions (11,118 -> 14,557) with 80 DTE still on the clock - a classic Protection-zone insurance build, not a pin - and today's cumulative reading stays net short gamma 34.1 points under the 1100 flip, so a debit spread rides that same hedging flow at defined, capped cost.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid to enter (last-price debit approx 7.0 pts x 200 baht/pt = approx 1,400 baht per spread); no further margin exposure.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close back above the 1080 call wall without a matching put-OI build would signal the protection thesis is fading, not the rally stalling.

strategies.name: Call debit spread 1080C / 1110C
strategies.rationale: The 1080 call wall (OI 1,878, +10.5% over 5 sessions, 264 lots today) is the nearest live resistance just 1.3% above spot; a confirmed break on rising volume would push spot through the 1100-1110 gamma-flip zone where dealers turn long gamma, so a debit spread captures that momentum at defined risk rather than fading it.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid to enter (last-price debit approx 13.4 pts x 200 baht/pt = approx 2,680 baht per spread); no further margin exposure.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close back below 1050 (today's max pain) invalidates the breakout attempt and favors a fade back toward the pain anchor.

S50U26.prediction: Bias is neutral with a mild bullish tilt while spot narrows the gap to the 1100 cumulative gamma flip (34.1 points, down from 44.9 on 07-10) and holds above the 1050 max-pain anchor; the locally call-heavy 1040-1110 band (+4,418 OI tilt) has kept the tape range-bound under the 1080 call wall for a third straight day. A daily close above 1080 on rising call volume would test the 1100-1110 flip/25-delta-call band and could shift the book toward net long gamma; a reversal back below roughly 1040-1050, where the near-put wall and max pain now sit together, would risk resuming the short-gamma acceleration seen on 07-09. At 80 DTE, treat directional conviction as low.
S50U26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice, and nothing here should be read as a signal to execute a position. SET50 index options are cash-settled on the index with no physical delivery, so any pull toward max pain (1050) or the 1100 gamma flip is a tendency, not a guarantee, and pinning mechanics here are structurally weaker than for physically-settled single stocks. This series is 80 days from expiry with OI still building, so directional conviction should stay low, and defined-risk structures still carry their full stated max loss.
